subject.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context

question: Should OpenClaw accept this custom cooperative glob walker and between-handler bootstrap yielding as the permanent compatibility boundary for existing bootstrap context behavior?
rationale: The patch is technically sound and well covered, but tests cannot fully settle whether replacing Node glob traversal and introducing event-loop interleavings between context-mutating hooks is an acceptable long-term runtime contract.

options.title: Accept the compatibility boundary
options.body: Approve the custom walker and bootstrap-only scheduling behavior, then merge after exact-head checks remain green.

options.title: Narrow the implementation first
options.body: Require a smaller cooperative approach or additional parity mechanism that retains more of Node's glob implementation and existing hook atomicity before merge.

options.title: Pause the PR
options.body: Keep current-main behavior until maintainers choose a different architecture for cooperative or off-main-thread bootstrap preparation.

recommendation.title: Accept the compatibility boundary
recommendation.body: Approve the custom walker and bootstrap-only scheduling behavior, then merge after exact-head checks remain green.

likelyOwner.reason: The boundary-safe bootstrap reader and much of the central bootstrap runtime history trace to their merged work, making them the strongest available owner for this compatibility choice.
